title: Patient Payment Plan Balance Adjustments and Collections Protection
content:
**Patient Accounts posting reference — reductions of a Patient Payment Plan balance without a patient payment**

The plan balance of a Patient Payment Plan is reduced without a patient payment only in the situations below, each recorded as its own adjustment.

| Adjustment | Situation | Amount removed from the plan balance |
|---|---|---|
| Insurance payment received | Where the tier provides that a later payer payment reduces the plan, a payer payment arrives later on an enrolled charge | The amount the patient no longer owes |
| Hardship discount | A Patient Hardship Discount Program approval applies to enrolled charges | The discount on those charges |
| Billing error correction | An enrolled charge is found to be overstated | The excess |
| Fee waiver | A late fee is waived | The waived fee |
| Returned to account | On default, where the tier returns a defaulted plan's balance to statements, or on patient cancellation, where the tier returns the balance on cancellation | The whole remaining balance, returned to the plans of care; each enrolled charge's unpaid part is re-posted there |

## Further clauses

1. While a plan is active or past due, its enrolled charges are never transferred to collections where the tier provides collections protection.
2. After an adjustment the installment is recomputed only at the patient's request, under the payment schedule terms of the Patient Payment Plan.

## Illustration (hypothetical figures)

An enrolled coinsurance charge of 180.00 is later paid in part by the payer, leaving the patient owing 60.00. Where the tier provides that a later payer payment reduces the plan, the plan balance is reduced by 120.00 as an insurance payment received. The installment is not recomputed unless the patient asks.
